S.3K.title: Route K: #Sha[3^infinity] <= 9 without the main conjecture
S.3K.statement: #Sha(E/Q)[3^infinity] <= 9; hence, with S.3L, Sha(E/Q)[3^infinity] is isomorphic to (Z/3)^2, with no Skinner, Skinner-Urban or GRH input. At the nonsplit multiplicative prime 3, T = T_3E is an extension of Z_3(eta) by T^0 = Z_3(1)(x)eta, with eta the unramified quadratic character (a_3 = -1). The eta-twist of Kobayashi's Coleman map for the Tate curve is an integral Coleman map H^1_Iw(Q_3,T)/H^1_Iw(Q_3,T^0) -> Lambda; it is an isomorphism and sends Kato's zeta element to the 3-adic L-function L_3 (alpha = -1, Neron differential). Kato's Poitou-Tate sequence (14.9.3, 17.10, the 17.13 template) with Kato 13.4(3) via 13.14 (the integral inequality at every height-one prime; H^2_loc = 0 at nonsplit 3) gives char(X) | L_3, where X is the dual of the classical 3^infinity-Selmer group over the cyclotomic Z_3-extension. Since rank E(Q) = 2 and v_3(a_2) = 2, f_E = T^2 g with v_3(g(0)) <= 2, and Jones 1989 Theorem 3.1 (forward), with v_3 = 0 for the gamma-normalized det<,>_gamma, gives #Sha[3^infinity] <= 9.

\begin{theorem}[\cid{S.3K}; written derivation; three model readers (one cross-model: Fable 5.1; two independent fresh sessions: Opus 5.5); all Anthropic models, not cross-family; no human review]\label{thm:routek}
$\#\Sha[3^\infty]\le9$. Hence, with Theorem~\ref{thm:sha3lower}, $\Sha[3^\infty]\simeq(\Z/3)^2$, with no input from Skinner, Skinner--Urban or GRH.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch (route K)]
Let $T=T_3E$, let $\Lambda=\Z_3[[\Gamma]]$ for the cyclotomic $\Z_3$-extension of $\Q$, and let $L_3$ be the $3$-adic $L$-function with $\alpha=a_3=-1$ and the N\'eron differential. The $3$-adic representation of $E$ is surjective onto $\GL_2(\Z_3)$ (Elkies's criterion \cite{elkies3}, computed), so Kato's image hypothesis (12.5.2) holds at $3$.

\emph{The local construction.} At the nonsplit multiplicative prime $3$, $T$ is an extension of $\Z_3(\eta)$ by $T^0=\Z_3(1)\otimes\eta$, where $\eta$ is the unramified quadratic character. Twisting Kobayashi's Coleman map for the Tate curve \cite{kobayashi06} by $\eta$ gives an integral Coleman map
\[
\mathrm{Col}\colon H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\Q_3,T)/H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\Q_3,T^0)\longrightarrow\Lambda .
\]
It is an isomorphism. Indeed $H^2_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\Q_3,T^0)=0$, because $\eta$ stays nontrivial on the totally ramified cyclotomic tower; the formal group is free of rank one over each $\Z_3[\Gamma_n]$; and an explicit norm-compatible system has $\log c_0=3/2$, which generates $3\Z_3$. By Kato's explicit reciprocity law \cite[12.5(1)]{kato}, compared character by character with the construction of \cite[\S3.2]{sw}, $\mathrm{Col}$ sends Kato's zeta element to $L_3$; in particular $L_3\in\Lambda$.

\emph{The global step.} Kato's Poitou--Tate sequence \cite[14.9.3 and 17.10]{kato}, arranged as in his \S17.13, gives an exact sequence
\[
0\to H^1(T)/Z\to\Lambda/(L_3)\to X\to H^2(T)\to0 ,
\]
where $X$ is the Pontryagin dual of the Selmer group over the cyclotomic $\Z_3$-extension. It is the classical Selmer group, because the local condition at $3$ is the image of $T^0$, and it is primitive at $5843$. Since $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(T)=0$ at the nonsplit prime $3$, Kato's Theorem~13.4(3), applied through 13.14, gives the integral inequality $\mathrm{length}\,H^2(T)_{\mathfrak p}\le\mathrm{length}\,(H^1(T)/Z)_{\mathfrak p}$ at every height-one prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\Lambda$, including $(3)$. Hence $f_E:=\mathrm{char}_\Lambda X$ divides $L_3$ in $\Lambda$.

\emph{Assembly.} Since $\rank E(\Q)=2$, the control argument gives $\ord_Tf_E\ge2$. As $\ord_3a_2=2$ (the certificate in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:sha3}), $L_3=T^2h$ and $f_E=T^2g$ with $g\mid h$, so $\ord_3g(0)\le2$ and $\Sha[3^\infty]$ is finite. Jones's leading-term theorem \cite[Thm.~3.1]{jones}, in its forward direction, gives
\[
g(0)=\text{unit}\cdot\frac{\#\Sha[3^\infty]\cdot\prod_\ell c_\ell\cdot\Reg_\gamma}{\#E(\Q)[3^\infty]^2}.
\]
Here $\Reg_\gamma=\det\langle\,,\rangle_\gamma$ is the $\gamma$-normalized regulator, which carries Jones's factor $(\log_3\kappa(\gamma))^{-r}$ with $\ord_3\log_34=1$. The height certificate gives $\ord_3\Reg_\gamma=0$. For the $\gamma$-free determinant, whose valuation is $2$, the chain would give only $\#\Sha[3^\infty]\le81$. The Tamagawa product $16$ and $E(\Q)_{\mathrm{tors}}=\Z/2$ are prime to $3$, so $\#\Sha[3^\infty]\le9$.
\end{proof}

## Route-K addendum (follow-on commit on `v0.2.5-bank`)

1. **S.3K (route K), Theorem `thm:routek`.** `#Sha[3^∞] ≤ 9`; with S.3L, `Sha[3^∞] ≅ (Z/3)²`. No Skinner, Skinner–Urban or
   GRH input. Grade label: written derivation; three model readers (one cross-model: Fable 5.1; two independent fresh
   sessions: Opus 5.5); all Anthropic models, not cross-family; no human review.
   - Local: at nonsplit 3, T is an extension of Z₃(η) by T⁰ = Z₃(1)⊗η. The η-twist of Kobayashi's Tate-curve Coleman map is
     an isomorphism `H¹_Iw(Q₃,T)/H¹_Iw(Q₃,T⁰) → Λ` that sends Kato's zeta element to L₃ (α = −1, ω_E). The χ convention is
     taken from Kato 12.5(1) and SW §3.2 (no involution).
   - Global: Kato 14.9.3, 17.10 and the 17.13 template, with Kato 13.4(3) via 13.14 (the integral inequality at every
     height-one prime; H²_loc = 0 at nonsplit 3), give char X | L₃ for the classical Selmer group.
   - Assembly: ord_T ≥ 2 (rank 2) and v₃(a₂) = 2 give v₃(g(0)) ≤ 2. Jones Thm 3.1 (forward) then gives the bound, with
     v₃ = 0 for the γ-normalized det⟨,⟩_γ (Jones's (log₃κ(γ))^{−r}; v₃(log₃4) = 1). The γ-free determinant has v₃ = 2 and
     would give only ≤ 81.
   - Inputs: ρ₃ surjective onto GL₂(Z₃) (Elkies criterion, computed; completeness SECONDARY); the height and a_{4,2}
     certificates; S.3L. Errata E1–E7 of the three readings are applied; none changes the bound.
2. **S.3.** Its statement and `grades` list are unchanged. Route K is its primary support, with the label above. Skinner
   2016 Thm A, as printed, is the second route, with two open steps for this curve: MS-13.4.1(ii) and MS-B1.
   LEAN_CHECKED covers the second route's deduction only.
3. **E1 citation fix.** Every citation of 12.5(4) as the integral step now reads Kato 13.4(3) via 13.14; 12.5(4) is printed for V.
   The fix covers the claims spec (hence CLAIM_INDEX, claims.json and the synthesis brief, all regenerated), §4 of the
   paper and this file. The checker scans every file in the manifest. A line that cites that item must also say that it
   is printed for V, except in this declared allowlist of historical records:

   - `review/history/**`;

   - `tools/verify_v025k_transition.py` (it holds the pattern).
4. **Ota.** S.17-47 now cites the print, Amer. J. Math. 140 (2018) 495–542, beside arXiv:1509.00682v1 (the text read). The
   theorem numbering was not re-checked against the print. The IMPORTED_PREPRINT label is kept. One evidence description
